item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q006_ubiquitin_like_function_divergence","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, Ubiquitin-related domains (family d.15.1.1; SUNID 54237), UBX domains (d.15.1.2; SUNID 54250), and Ras-binding domains/RBDs (d.15.1.5; SUNID 54263) are distinct families within the same Ubiquitin-like superfamily (d.15.1; SUNID 54236), beta-Grasp fold (d.15), and alpha+beta class (d). Their common superfamily placement supports distant homology/common ancestry and a conserved beta-grasp structural core—not merely analogous folding—but their separation into families records substantial functional divergence. Thus cross-family structures can help recognize or model the conserved core when closer templates are unavailable, but family-specific representatives should be preferred; no representative from one family stands for the functions, interfaces, flexible loops, or whole-protein context of all three. It would be unsafe to transfer ubiquitin conjugation/tagging, C-terminal conjugation chemistry, or E1/E2/E3-pathway roles to UBX or RBD domains; to transfer UBX-specific p97/VCP-adaptor binding to ubiquitin-related or RBD domains; or to infer Ras binding, effector specificity, or signaling function for ubiquitin-related or UBX domains. Even within the RBD family, the label alone does not establish binding to a particular Ras-family GTPase. Such functional assignments require independent family-sensitive sequence/phylogenetic evidence, conserved interface or motif evidence, relevant complex structures, and biochemical binding or conjugation data. SCOPe classifies the domain, so these conclusions also must not be extended automatically to every domain or activity of the containing protein.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info: /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope__search_scop: /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=Ubiquitin-related&mode=auto&limit=50; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=UBX&mode=token&limit=50; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=RBD&mode=auto&limit=50","mcp__scope__get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54236; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54236/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54236/homology; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54237; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54237/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54250; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54250/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54263; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/54263/parents"]}]}
